subject.title: [Feature]: Two-tier agent capabilities: session self-service tools + OpenClaw system-agent delegation (Crestodian rename)

question: Should the canonical agent authority model allow direct writes only within an agent's own session while requiring host-verified human approval through the OpenClaw system agent for every persistent system change?
rationale: This defines the permanent trust boundary for configuration, provider authentication, plugins, channels, updates, and restarts; implementation evidence cannot substitute for maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Approve two-tier authority
options.body: Sponsor the phased design with session-scoped direct tools and mandatory host-verified approval for persistent system writes.

options.title: Limit scope to sessions
options.body: Implement session self-service first while deferring system-agent delegation and gateway default changes to a separate architecture decision.

options.title: Keep system changes operator-only
options.body: Retain Control UI and operator-driven system configuration without adding agent-to-system-agent delegation.

recommendation.title: Approve two-tier authority
recommendation.body: Sponsor the phased design with session-scoped direct tools and mandatory host-verified approval for persistent system writes.
